sections.content: A news account becomes easier to follow when events are ordered with connectors. You know *primero*, *después* and *finalmente* from A2 Unit 28, *mientras* from A2 Unit 13 and *después de* + infinitive from A2 Unit 4. New here is *posteriormente*, a more formal way to say “later”. *Primero* introduces the first stage, *posteriormente* or *después* moves the account forward, and *finalmente* closes it. *Mientras* and *por eso* also show relationships between events.

items.spanish: Primero llegó la información de los testigos; posteriormente apareció una grabación.
items.english: First the information from witnesses arrived; later a recording appeared.

items.spanish: Mientras los periodistas investigaban, comenzaron a circular nuevos rumores.
items.english: While journalists were investigating, new rumours began to circulate.

items.spanish: Después de ver el vídeo, más personas contaron lo que habían visto.
items.english: After seeing the video, more people told what they had seen.

items.spanish: Finalmente, los investigadores explicaron qué había sucedido.
items.english: Finally, the investigators explained what had happened.

sections.content: Use sequencing connectors to make the order of events explicit. This is especially useful when several past actions appear in the same report.
